newsitem.title: CANADA: Bre-X still awaiting Indonesian response.
newsitem.headline: Bre-X still awaiting Indonesian response.

text.p: Bre-X Minerals Ltd and Barrick Gold Corp are still waiting for word from the Indonesian government about their proposal to divide up the huge Busang gold deposit, Bre-X said on Monday.
"We're awaiting response from the government," Bre-X spokesman Steve McAnulty said in a phone interview from Calgary.
Bre-X and Barrick said last week they had submitted a joint proposal to the Indonesian government to split the Busang gold find, but Bre-X said it needed clarification on a few issues.
The companies said they would wait until they had heard from the Indonesian government to announce the terms of the proposed deal.
McAnulty said they had had no indication about when a repsonse would come.
But Indonesia's Mines Minister, Ida Bagus Sudjana, said in Jakarta on Monday that he was in the dark about the deal between the two companies.
"They haven't reported to me yet. If they do, I will ask them to make an announcement (of their deal), that you have a deal with each other," he told reporters.
But Bre-X confirmed the joint submission was delivered to the Mines Ministry's secretary-general, Umar Said, on December 16.

"Perhaps it hasn't reached the minister's desk yet," he said. "We are operating under the assumption that we have a joint proposal with Barrick before the government, which we would expect to be approved."

Bre-X shares were among the heaviest traded on the Toronto Stock Exchange on Monday morning, with 730,000 shares trading hands. The stock was up C$0.45 to 22.45. Barrick fell C$0.05 to 39.70 after the first two hours of trading.
Bre-X stock has been rising steadily since Bre-X chief executive officer David Walsh expressed enthusiasm about the terms of the proposed deal.
Walsh told Reuters last week that Bre-X shareholders would not be disappointed with the deal and that his negotiators have been able to "substantially enhance the Barrick offer."
The Indonesian government told the two companies last month to form a joint venture to develop the Busang deposit, estimated to contain at least 57 million ounces of gold.
Umar said the companies had agreed to a split which would give Barrick 67.5 percent, Bre-X 22.5 percent and the Indonesian government a 10 percent stake.
Sudjana said on Monday about the 10 percent stake: "We will later bring out the funds and invest as well."
Barrick officials were not available for comment Monday.
